text: Loss of a glutamic acid in the AAA-ATPase torsinA causes most early-onset autosomal dominant primary dystonia. Snapin, which binds SNAP-25 and enhances SNARE–synaptotagmin association, interacts with wild-type and mutant torsinA, co-localizing with torsinA on PC12 dense core granules and in perinuclear inclusions containing DeltaE-torsinA in SH-SY5Y cells. FM1-43 and anti-synaptotagmin I assays showed wild-type torsinA overexpression inhibits synaptic vesicle endocytosis, while DeltaE-torsinA increases FM1-43 uptake; siRNA knockdown of snapin and/or torsinA similarly inhibited exo-endocytosis, and torsinA downregulation left synaptotagmin I on the plasma membrane. TorsinA thus acts with snapin in regulated exocytosis; DeltaE-torsinA acts by loss of function, possibly impairing dopamine uptake in dystonia. VAP (VAPA/VAPB), an ER-anchored tethering protein, regulates endosomal PI4P, affecting WASH-dependent actin nucleation and retromer function. VAP is recruited to retromer budding sites via SNX2; VAP-lacking cells accumulate PI4P, actin comets and trans-Golgi proteins on endosomes, mimicked by OSBP downregulation.
